_note: proof-decomposer's checked-in routing corpus. This is a LEXICAL-OVERLAP legibility aid, NOT a verdict — routing-eval.py measures token overlap between a phrase and the description only. Positives span the invocation families (imperative 'state/grade this proof', diagnostic 'is this valid', symptom 'circular step / find a counterexample', object-first 'this argument', plus 2-3 indirect paraphrases). The indirect/paraphrase positives are deliberately low-overlap and MAY score recall 0 here — that is a proxy limit, not a description defect. Negatives are drawn ADVERSARIALLY from CONFUSABLE in-repo siblings: proof shares 'is this right / check this / decompose & grade on two axes' with code-decomposer (a unit of code) and type-decomposer (types/schemas) but is otherwise distinct, plus a math-but-out-of-scope item (theorem-proving / primality search) the skill explicitly DEFERS — it grades a GIVEN argument, never searches for one. Each negative belongs to a NAMED sibling. Re-derive when the neighbourhood changes.
